questions.question: Describe the Earth's position in the Solar System and state its average distance from the Sun. Explain what causes the seasons, and why the changing distance from the Sun does not.
questions.expected_answer: The Earth is the third planet from the Sun, after Mercury and Venus, at an average distance of about 150 million km (one astronomical unit); sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach it. Its orbit is nearly circular, varying only between about 147 and 152 million km. The seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis (about 23.5°), which changes how directly the Sun's rays strike each hemisphere during the year. The distance change is too small to matter; the Earth is actually closest to the Sun during the Southern Hemisphere summer.

questions.question: Explain why liquid water is essential for life, and what is meant by the habitable zone. Explain why the Moon has no liquid water even though it is the same distance from the Sun as the Earth.
questions.expected_answer: Water dissolves and transports substances in organisms, takes part in reactions such as photosynthesis and makes up most of the mass of cells (about 60% of the human body). It is liquid only between 0 °C and 100 °C at normal pressure. The habitable zone is the region around a star where a planet's temperature allows liquid water on its surface; Earth lies within it. The Moon is too small: its weak gravity cannot hold an atmosphere, and without atmospheric pressure liquid water evaporates into space; its temperature also swings from about 120 °C to about -170 °C.

questions.question: List the conditions on Earth that support life. For the atmosphere, explain the natural greenhouse effect and the role of the ozone layer, and use Venus and Mars to show what happens when the atmosphere is too thick or too thin.
questions.expected_answer: Conditions: distance from the Sun in the habitable zone allowing liquid water; enough mass and gravity to hold an atmosphere; an atmosphere with oxygen, carbon dioxide and nitrogen; a natural greenhouse effect keeping the average temperature at about 15 °C instead of about -18 °C; an ozone layer absorbing most harmful ultraviolet radiation; a magnetic field (from the molten iron outer core) deflecting the solar wind; and a stable Sun supplying energy. Venus has a very thick atmosphere of about 96% carbon dioxide (about 90 times Earth's surface pressure), causing a runaway greenhouse effect and about 460 °C, hotter than Mercury. Mars has an atmosphere less than 1% as thick as Earth's, holds little heat and is very cold, so water cannot stay liquid on its surface for long.
